module_title: Banking and Financial Awareness: BASEL Norms and NPA Management (Level 2: Intermediate)
introduction: This intermediate level delves into the classification of NPAs (Sub-standard, Doubtful, Loss), the tools banks use to recover money (SARFAESI Act), and the primary pillars of the first two Basel accords (Basel I and Basel II). This is critical for IBPS PO and SBI PO exams.

core_concepts.title: Classification of NPAs
core_concepts.description:
Once a loan becomes an NPA, it is categorized based on time:
1. Sub-standard Asset: An NPA that has remained in this category for a period less than or equal to 12 months.
2. Doubtful Asset: An asset that has remained in the sub-standard category for a period of more than 12 months.
3. Loss Asset: An asset where the loss has been identified by the bank or internal/external auditors or the RBI, and it is considered uncollectible.

core_concepts.title: SARFAESI Act 2002
core_concepts.description: This is the 'ultimate weapon' for banks. It allows banks to auction residential or commercial properties to recover loans without the intervention of the court. The bank must serve a 60-day notice to the defaulter before taking possession of the collateral.

core_concepts.title: Basel I and Basel II
core_concepts.description:
- Basel I (1988): Focused almost entirely on 'Credit Risk' (risk of default). It set the minimum capital requirement at 8%.
- Basel II (2004): Introduced a more comprehensive framework based on 3 Pillars:
  1. Minimum Capital Requirements
  2. Supervisory Review Process
  3. Market Discipline.

important_entities.name: ARC (Asset Reconstruction Company) / Bad Banks
important_entities.key_fact: Specialized financial institutions that buy NPAs (Bad Loans) from banks.
important_entities.significance: ARCs purchase bad loans from commercial banks at a mutually agreed discounted price. This cleans up the bank's balance sheet, allowing the bank to focus on normal banking operations and fresh lending, while the ARC focuses on recovering the money.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
A common trap in 'Statement-based' questions: The SARFAESI Act DOES NOT apply to:
1. Agricultural land.
2. Loans where the outstanding principal is less than ₹1 Lakh.
3. Loans where the remaining debt is less than 20% of the original principal.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: C = Capital Requirement, S = Supervisory Review, M = Market Discipline. PO exams frequently ask 'Which of the following is NOT a pillar of Basel II?'

exam_strategy_tips: Before a loan becomes an NPA (the 90-day window), it is classified as an SMA (Special Mention Account). Memorize the exact brackets: SMA-0 (1-30 days), SMA-1 (31-60 days), and SMA-2 (61-90 days).
